01.actor: A man who deposited sesame plants, and the friend who held them
01.event: A depositor asked for his sesame plants back and the bailee claimed he had already taken them.
01.turn: The owner pointed to the barrel of the stated amount at the bailee's house; the bailee said those were other plants.
01.outcome: The dispute went before the Sages, where Rav Hisda would rely on the owner's description and Rava rejected that; no verdict is told.
01.summary: A man deposited sesame plants with a friend. When he asked for them back, the friend said he had already taken them. The owner pointed to a barrel of a particular amount in the friend's house, but the friend said those were different plants. The case went to the Sages, but no ruling on the facts is reported.
01.missing: The actual ruling or what became of the sesame; only the scholars' competing arguments follow.

02.event: She seized a saddlebag full of coins for her sustenance.
02.turn: The Sages found they had no power to take it from her.
02.summary: Rav Dimi reported an incident from Eretz Yisrael. Rabbi Shabbtai's daughter-in-law seized a saddlebag full of coins to cover her sustenance. The Sages had no power to remove it from her, so she kept it.

03.actor: The sons of the house of bar Tzartzur, and Rav Amram
03.event: The sons of two wives disputed an estate that had grown in value, and came before Rav Amram.
03.turn: Rav Amram told one side to appease the other; they ignored him and he threatened excommunication, then sent them to Rav Naham.
03.outcome: Rav Naham ruled that the heirs had acquired their rights when the father died, so they divide the estate equally.
03.summary: The sons of two wives of bar Tzartzur came to Rav Amram over an estate that had appreciated. He told them to appease the other sons, but they ignored him, so he threatened to excommunicate them and sent them to Rav Nahman. Rav Nahman ruled that, as with a depreciated estate, the heirs acquired rights at the father's death, so they divide equally.

04.event: Sent to betroth a woman for his son, he betrothed her to himself.
04.turn: This looked like deceit by an agent; the explanation is that her family would not give her to the son and he feared someone else would betroth her while he reported back.
04.outcome: The betrothal stood and his conduct was justified.
04.summary: Ravin the Pious went to betroth a woman for his son but betrothed her to himself. The Gemara objects that this is deceit, then explains that her family would not give her to the son. Ravin did not go back to tell his son because someone else might have betrothed her meanwhile.

05.event: Rav Beivai told the Sages not to trust Rav Yosef's report of a teaching.
05.turn: Rav Beivai said he had taught it in the name of Rav Adda bar Ahava with a different reasoning; Rav Yosef realized he had confused rabbim with Rabbi.
05.summary: Rav Yosef had reported a teaching in the name of Rabbi. Rav Beivai told the Sages not to listen, saying he had taught it to Rav Yosef in the name of Rav Adda bar Ahava, and the word was rabbim, many. Rav Yosef exclaimed in astonishment that he had mistaken one word for the other.

06.actor: Rav Yosef and his student Abaye
06.event: Rav Yosef said he had never heard Shmuel's teaching on roofs, and Abaye reminded him that he himself had taught it.
06.turn: Rav Yosef remembered, but corrected how the teaching had been transmitted.
06.outcome: Rav Yosef restated the teaching, and when Abaye pressed on the word residents, clarified that too.
06.summary: Rav Yosef, whose memory had been affected by illness, said he had not heard Shmuel's teaching about roofs. Abaye reminded him that he had taught it and had even added a qualification. Rav Yosef then recalled it, but with a different wording of the qualification, and answered Abaye's objection by explaining how his word residents should be read.

08.event: Ravina arranged for Rav Ashi's daughter to collect one-tenth of an estate, from one heir as intermediate land without an oath and from an orphan as inferior land with an oath.
08.outcome: The differing treatment is taken as proof she was a creditor of the sons.
08.summary: Ravina had Rav Ashi's daughter collect her one-tenth of an estate from two heirs. From Mar she collected intermediate-quality land without an oath, and from an orphan son of Rav Sama she collected inferior land with an oath. This is used as proof of whose creditor she is.
08.missing: Why the heirs stood where they did, and any conflict or turn; it is reported as a precedent.

10.actor: A man who sold land, and Rav Pappa
10.event: A man sold land to Rav Pappa to buy oxen, then did not need the money.
10.turn: He regretted the sale and asked for it back.
10.outcome: Rav Pappa returned the land, though beyond the letter of the law.
10.summary: A man sold land to Rav Pappa because he needed money to buy oxen. In the end he did not need the money and regretted the sale, and Rav Pappa gave the land back. The Gemara notes that Rav Pappa acted beyond what the law required.

12.actor: Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
12.event: Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba found Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi hurrying his grandchild to the synagogue with a cloth thrown over his head.
12.turn: Rabbi Yehoshua explained that a verse links teaching children to the day at Sinai.
12.outcome: Rabbi Hiyya and Rabba bar Rav Huna each adopted the practice of teaching a child before eating.
12.summary: Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba met Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi rushing a child to the synagogue with a covering hastily on his head and asked what the fuss was about. Rabbi Yehoshua answered that the verse about making things known to your sons is joined to the day at Sinai. From then on Rabbi Hiyya would not eat until he had taught a child, and Rabba bar Rav Huna would not eat until he had brought a child to the study hall.

13.event: Rabbi Zeira, finding no ferry, crossed the Jordan holding a rope when going up to Eretz Yisrael.
13.turn: A Sadducee mocked him as hasty.
13.outcome: Rabbi Zeira answered that Moses and Aaron did not merit entering, so he hurried before anything could prevent him.
13.summary: Rabbi Zeira went up to Eretz Yisrael and, with no ferry, crossed the Jordan by holding a rope. A Sadducee mocked him as the hasty people who said do before hear. Rabbi Zeira replied that even Moses and Aaron did not merit entering, so he did not know he would, and he hurried.

14.event: He left for the study hall without waiting for Rabbi Shimon bar Yohai and stayed twelve years.
14.turn: On return he did not recognize his town and was led home by hearing his daughter called; his wife saw him and died of shock.
14.outcome: He pleaded for mercy and she was revived.
14.summary: Rabbi Hananya ben Hakhinai would not wait for Rabbi Shimon's wedding feast to end and went to study for twelve years. He came back to a town whose paths had changed and sat by the river, where he heard a girl called Hakhinai's daughter and followed her home. His wife looked up, saw him, and died from the shock. He prayed for her and she came back to life.

15.actor: Rav Pappa and Yehuda bar Mareimar
15.event: Rav Pappa went to write his son's bride's marriage contract and Yehuda bar Mareimar came to greet him but would not enter the house.
15.turn: Rav Pappa pressed him in; Yehuda bar Mareimar sat silent, and the bride's father took his silence for anger.
15.outcome: The bride's father wrote over everything he owned as her dowry and told him he had left nothing for himself.
15.summary: Rav Pappa went to have his son's marriage contract written, and Yehuda bar Mareimar came to greet him but would not go in. Rav Pappa eventually got him to enter, where he sat silent. The bride's father, Abba of Sura, took the silence for anger and wrote all he had as the dowry, saying at last that he had left himself nothing.

16.actor: Rabbi Tarfon, Rabbi Akiva and the Elders
16.event: The Elders gathered in a loft in Lod and were asked whether study or action is greater.
16.turn: Rabbi Tarfon said action and Rabbi Akiva said study.
16.outcome: All concluded that study is greater because it leads to action.
16.summary: Rabbi Tarfon and the Elders were reclining in a loft in Lod when they were asked whether study or action is greater. Rabbi Tarfon said action, Rabbi Akiva said study, and in the end everyone agreed study is greater since it leads to action.
16.missing: Anything beyond a debate that ends in agreement; it is a scene with a verdict rather than an event with a turn.

17.actor: A steward for a dead man's orphans, before Abaye
17.event: A man had set up a field as a marker for another, later contested it, and died; his steward came before Abaye.
17.turn: Abaye said the man had lost his right; the steward argued what the father would have claimed, one furrow and then repurchase.
17.outcome: Abaye accepted the claims, gave the other side one furrow, and let the steward keep the palm-tree furrow, praising his skill.
17.summary: A man had listed a field as a marker for someone else, then contested it and died. His steward came before Abaye, who first said the man had lost his right. The steward argued what the father could have claimed, a single furrow and later repurchase, and Abaye accepted both. The steward kept the furrow with the palm trees, and Abaye praised appointing a steward like him.

18.event: A student of Rabbi Eliezer was liable to death by burning for sins against God.
18.turn: The Rabbis said to leave him alone.
18.outcome: He was spared because he had served a great person.
18.summary: Rabbi Eliezer had a student who was liable to be burned for his sins against God. The Rabbis said to leave him alone because he had served a great man, and he was spared.
18.missing: What the student did and how the matter came before the Rabbis; only the verdict is given.

19.actor: Rabbi Hanina bar Hama, Rabbi Afes and Levi
19.event: Rabbi Hanina refused the appointment to head the yeshiva out of deference to the older Rabbi Afes, who took the seat while he and Levi studied outside.
19.turn: Rabbi Afes died and Rabbi Hanina took the head seat, leaving Levi with no one to study with.
19.outcome: Levi went to Babylonia, where Rav inferred these events from Levi's ruling.
19.summary: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi appointed Hanina bar Hama head of the yeshiva, but Hanina refused out of respect for Rabbi Afes, who was older. Afes sat at the head while Hanina sat outside with Levi. When Afes died, Hanina took the head seat and Levi had no one to study with, so he went to Babylonia, and Rav deduced all this when he heard of a limping scholar there.

20.actor: A man who betrothed a woman in her waiting period, and Rafram
20.event: A man betrothed a woman within three months of her divorce or widowhood and fled.
20.outcome: Rafram ruled that his flight was sufficient punishment.
20.summary: A man betrothed a woman during the three months after her divorce or husband's death, which is forbidden, and then fled. When an incident like this came before Rafram, he said the man's flight was punishment enough and he was not excommunicated.
20.missing: Who the man was and what led to the incident; the passage mostly states a dispute between Rav Aha and Rafram.
